texto: Le taux de globules blancs indexé est le principal facteur pronostique des LAM t(8;21). La translocation t(8;21) est l'anomalie chromosomique la plus frequente des leucemies aigues myeloblastiques. Cependant peu d'etudes ont ete consacrees aux facteurs pronostiques dans cette variete de LAM. L'intergroupe francais des LAM a donc realise une etude retrospective de 161 patients presentant une LAM avec t(8;21), qui avaient ete inclus de facon prospective dans 6 essais therapeutiques entre 1987 et 1998 (LAME-91, ALFA-9000, BGMT-87, BGMT-91, GOELAM-01 et GOELAM-02). Les facteurs pronostiques ont ete etudies chez les 154 patients mis en remission complete. La survie sans maladie (DFS) et la survie globale (OS) a 5 ans sont de 52 et 59 % respectivement, sans etre influencees par le traitement de consolidation qu'il s'agisse d'allogreffe ou de chimiotherapie. En analyse univariee, ni l'âge, ni le sexe, ni la presence d'une localisation extra-medullaire, ni la presence d'anomalies cytogenetiques additionnelles ne modifient la DFS ou l'OS. On constate cependant une tendance a l'augmentation de la DFS quand le pourcentage de blastes medullaires est bas et qu'il persiste des metaphases normales, sans que ces constatations n'atteignent la significativite. Le seul facteur pronostique identifie comme significatif pour la DFS comme pour l'OS est le taux de globules blancs. Afin de tenir compte du potentiel de differenciation granuleuse du clone leucemique, un taux de globules blancs indexe a ete defini comme etant le produit de la leucocytose par le pourcentage de blastes medullaires. Ce taux de globules blancs indexe permet de mieux evaluer le pronostic que la leucocytose seule grâce a une classification en 3 groupes de pronostic tres different comme le montre le tableau ci-dessous : En analyse multivariee, ce taux de globules blancs indexe reste le seul facteur pronostique pour la DFS (p = 0,003), la duree de remission complete (p = 0,002) et la survie (p = 0,04). La valeur du taux de globules blancs indexe pourrait expliquer l'heterogeneite du pronostic de ces LAM t(8;21) et le plus mauvais pronostic chez les enfants qui ont un taux de GB indexe plus eleve que celui des adultes (un des essais etait pediatrique). La prise en charge therapeutique pourrait donc etre stratifiee en fonction de ce taux de globules blancs indexe. Les resultats du traitement de ces LAM pourraient etre ameliores en combinant le G-CSF a la chimiotherapie, car le G-CSF induit la maturation des cellules porteuses de la t(8;21) in vitro et in vivo. Mais en pratique si le taux de globules blancs est facile a mesurer, l'appreciation du nombre de blastes medullaires peut varier. Et comme le font remarquer les auteurs en conclusion, cette valeur pronostique du taux de globules blancs indexe doit etre confirmee par d'autres groupes menant des etudes cooperatives sur les LAM. 1. titulo: Cytological and Histopathological Correlation of Feline Giant Cell-Rich Osteosarcoma

texto: Cytological and Histopathological Correlation of Feline Giant Cell-Rich Osteosarcoma. Background: Primary bone tumours are uncommon and poorly reported in cats but osteosarcoma (OSA) is the most frequent, mostly in elderly animals. Giant cell-rich OSA is considered rare in the literature representing 3% of all OSA in humans. The mitotic index seems to have a significant effect on the survival time of cats affected by this neoplasm as well as the tumour histopathological grade. The objective of this study was to report the cytological and histopathological findings of a giant cell rich OSA in a 4-year old cat with persistent feline leukemia virus (FeLV) antigenaemia.Case: A 4-year-old male neutered cat was referred with a history of persistent FeLV viraemia and pelvic limb lameness with a firm swelling. Previous radiographs of the affected limb revealed bone lysis in the third and fourth metatarsals and increased soft tissue radiopacity in the tarsal region. The referral veterinary assumed it to be osteomyelitis and initiated clinical treatment with antibiotic and anti-inflammatory. The cat was referred after there was no response to medical treatment. The cat was presented with a 5cm diameter ulcerated mass, with putrid odor in the pelvic limb. Complementary exams were performed, and abnormalities were found, including increased urea, creatinine, calcium and potassium, and decreased sodium and phosphorus. A new radiograph showed exuberant bone proliferation, with increased radiopacity involving tarsal, metatarsal, distal third of tarsal I and II, and distal diaphysis of metatarsal V, without compromising the metaphyseal region of distal diaphysis of metatarsal IV. Chest radiographs and abdominal ultrasound were unremarkable. Fine-needle aspiration was performed for cytological analysis, which reavealed a moderate amount of pleomorphic mesenchymal cells with moderate adhesion, cytoplasm with a format ranging from fusiform to stellate, pronounced anisocytosis and cellular pleomorphism, and elevated nucleus:cytoplasm ratio. Nucleus was oval and presented loose chromatin, single to double large and evident nucleolus, frequent karyomegaly, along with marked anisocariosis and nuclear pleomorphism. Multinucleated giant cells were and there was a single mitotic figure in 12 high power fields (0.196 mm2 FN20/400x). Therefore, it was suggestive of malignant mesenchymal neoplasia with possibility of OSA, fibrosarcoma oe undifferentiated sarcoma. Limb amputation with femoral disarticulation was performed uneventfully. The material was conserved in 10% formalin, submitted to macroscopic and microscopic evaluation, which showed a large number of fusiform and stellate cells, with indistinct edges, scarce eosinophilic cytoplasm, high nucleus:cytoplasm ratio and oval nucleus, presenting moderate to marked anisocariosis, loose chromatin, with unique and evident nucleoli, besides of bone trabeculae. Nuclear pleomorphism was moderate and there was four mitotic figures in three random high-power fields (400x). It was observed areas of vascular ectasia, and neoplastic embolization in lymphatic and blood vessels. Among the cells, collagenous stroma was predominant but in some areas there was an eosinophilic amorphous material with the possibility of osteoid matrix or collagen. There was also a large numbers of multinucleated giant cells. The histopathological result was compatible with a grade III giant cell rich OSA.Discussion: Although bone tumours are uncommon in cats, OSA is the most frequent, affecting maingly middle-aged to elderly cats, with a mean age of 10 years, which is different from the present report in a 4-year old cat, with FeLV persistent viraemia. Retroviral status may have influenced the development of the disease at na early onset. FeLV induces uncontrolled cell proliferation through insertional mutagenesis (usually near myc) inducing malignant neoplasias, mainly lymphoma, but also multiple cartilaginous exostosis, which, along with osteomyelitis and bone cyst were included in this patient´s list of differential diagnoses. Despite the macroscopic and radiographical andagressiveness there was no metastasis identified through chest radiographs or abdominal ultrasound, and feline OSA is associated with a lower metastatic rate, if compared to canine OSA. Cytological analysis was compatible with malignant mesenchymal neoplasia, being suggestive of giant cell rich OSA. There is no cytological classification for OSA, however cytological findings of malignancy may be correlated with the patient's clinical course. Cytological features were in agreement with the histopathological findings, compatible with a grade III giant cell rich OSA. Therefore, it is concluded that the characteristics of malignancy presented by cytology were sufficient for the recommendation of amputation of the affected limb, once there was no imaging sign of metastases in the chest or abdomen. giant cell-rich osteosarcoma feline leukemia virus cats fine needle aspiration cytology mitotic index histopathological grading primary bone tumors fibrosarcoma differential diagnosis survival time hypercalcemia

titulo: Profils d’expression des gènes dans le cancer du sein
keywords: breast cancer;gene expression profiling;BRCA1 mutation;BRCA2 mutation;hereditary breast cancer;early-onset breast cancer;gene expression signatures;tumor molecular classification;multidimensional scaling;DNA microarrays;cancer diagnosis
texto: Profils d’expression des gènes dans le cancer du sein. Al'origine, l'étude moléculaire des voies de la carcinogenèse s'est penchée sur un seul gène à la fois. De nouvelles techniques vont permettre de mesurer simultanément le niveau d'expression de milliers de gènes dans un fragment tumoral (profil transcriptionnel). Des travaux récents ont montré l'intérêt de ces techniques dans la classification des leucémies, des lymphomes, des mélanomes et des cancers du sein. Une proportion importante des cas familiaux de cancer du sein à début précoce sont dus à une mutation du gène BRCA1 ou BRCA2, mutations très rares dans les formes sporadiques. On peut imaginer que ces formes proviennent d'une perturbation des voies moléculaires auxquelles participent BRCA1 et BRCA2. Hedenfalk et al. [1] ont utilisé des chips d'ADN complémentaires contenant les sondes de 5361 gènes afin de comparer les profils transcriptionnels de 22 tumeurs du sein avec ou sans mutation des gènes BRCA1 ou BRCA2. Leur méthode comportait la comparaison de l'intensité de liaison d'un ADNc fluorescent généré par un ARN messager issu d'un tissu de référence et de la tumeur, à une rangée comportant des milliers d'ADNc clonés sur une lame de verre. Cette technique permet d'identifier les gènes actifs et silencieux dans les deux tissus. Pour visualiser les 22 fragments tumoraux dans un espace à 5361 dimensions, les auteurs ont utilisé une forme de réduction des données (échelonnage multidimensionnel) permettant d'en diminuer la complexité. Cela leur a permis de démontrer que les profils d'expression des trois types de tumeurs (BRCA1, BRCA2 ou aucun des deux) étaient clairement distincts. Ce travail illustre la possibilité d'une vision à l'échelle du génome dans le diagnostic de cancer. Des profils d'expressions génétiques complexes peuvent être utilisés pour identifier les anomalies de toute une voie moléculaire, sans qu'il soit nécessaire de rechercher le gène en cause. Cette étude illustre aussi la façon dont les difficultés représentées par le séquençage de grands gènes comme BRCA1 peuvent être partiellement contournées par l'utilisation du profil transcriptionnel. D'autres applications sont imaginables, par exemple l'utilisation de cette technique pour prédire la réponse d'une tumeur à la chimiothérapie, dans le cas des lymphomes par exemple [2]1. texto: Commentaire du travail de Larghi A et al., pp. 308. See also: Interobserver agreement and accuracy of preoperative endoscopic ultrasound-guided biopsy for histological grading of pancreatic cancer Endoscopy 2015; 47(04): 308-314 DOI: 10.1055/s-0034-1390912 Alberto Larghi, Loredana Correale, Riccardo Ricci, Ihab Abdulkader, Geneviève Monges, Julio Iglesias-Garcia, Marc Giovannini, Fabia Attili, Giovanna Vitale, Cesare Hassan, Guido Costamagna, Guido Rindi. Interobserver agreement and accuracy of preoperative endoscopic ultrasound-guided biopsy for histological grading of pancreatic cancer. Commentaires: Maxime Palazzo, Gilles Lesur, Julien Branche, Laurent Heyries Trente pour cent des patients ayant un adénocarcinome du pancréas réséqué d’emblée vont décéder dans l’année suivant la chirurgie en raison d’une récidive précoce. Une étude récente rétrospective a montré que le caractère peu différencié de la tumeur était associé à cette mortalité. La détermination préopératoire par la biopsie guidée par échoendoscopie du grade histologique pourrait permettre d’adapter la thérapeutique en proposant un traitement néo-adjuvant aux patients ayant un grade défavorable. Le but de cette étude était de déterminer la concordance inter-observateurs et la précision diagnostique de la biopsie guidée par échoendoscopie pour la détermination du grade histologique préopératoire de l’adénocarcinome du pancréas. Il s’agissait d’une étude européenne multicentrique, rétrospective incluant des patients opérés d’emblée d’un adénocarcinome du pancréas et ayant eu une biopsie préopératoire guidée par échoendoscopie à l’aiguille de 19 19 G. Le gold standard était le grade post-opératoire (compte-rendu anatomopathologique sans relecture protocolaire), les tumeurs étant classées comme bien, modérément, ou peu différenciées selon la classification OMS. Quatre anatomopathologistes expérimentés évaluaient en aveugle les lames préopératoires. La concordance inter-observateurs ainsi que la précision diagnostique de la biopsie pour le grade histologique étaient calculées. Quarante-deux patients étaient inclus entre février 2008 et avril 2013. Les tumeurs étaient bien, modérément ou peu différenciées dans 2 (4,8 %), 19 (45,2 %) et 21 (50 %) cas, respectivement. La concordance inter-observateurs était mauvaise avec un kappa à 0,27. La précision diagnostique globale était de 56 %. La précision diagnostique pour différencier les tumeurs bien/modérément vs peu différenciées était de 60 %. Il n’y avait pas de différence selon le type d’aiguille utilisée (procore vs standard). Au total, cette étude montre que la détermination préopératoire du grade histologique de l’adénocarcinome du pancréas par la biopsie guidée par échoendoscopie est de qualité insuffisante en raison d’une concordance inter-observateur mauvaise et d’une précision diagnostique moyenne. Cette information ne peut donc pas être utilisée en réunion de concertation pluridisciplinaire pour décider de la nécessité d’un traitement néo-adjuvant dans le cadre d’une lésion résécable d’emblée. pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma endoscopic ultrasound-guided biopsy histological grading interobserver agreement preoperative biopsy tumor differentiation neoadjuvant therapy pancreaticoduodenectomy diagnostic accuracy

texto: The Torah as a Structurally Constrained Morphological System: A Quantitative Study of Foundation-Letter Structure in Biblical Hebrew — Complete Research Package v3. This study presents a computational morphological analysis of the Torah (Five Books of Moses) as a closed linguistic corpus of 76,584 tokens. Every word is decomposed into three structural layers: a foundation root (semantic anchor), a mandatory root (stable consonantal skeleton), and an expansion layer (morphological extensions). CENTRAL FINDING: Morphological expansion is governed by a restricted "control alphabet" of 10 letters — EmetNiyahu (aleph, mem, tav, nun, yod, he, vav) plus BKL (bet, kaf, lamed) — accounting for 99.87% of all 97,599 extension tokens (p ≤ 0.0003, 0/10,000 random sets). KEY RESULTS (5-fold cross-validation, 98,122 annotated pairs): • Meaning prediction (root + YHW): 87.8% ± 0.2% • Meaning prediction (root + YHW + nikud): 92.1% ± 0.2% • YHW polysemy separation: 83.2% (93.2% with nikud) on 380 roots • AMTN parallel root system: 57.6% decomposition, 96.6% YHW separation (99.3% with nikud) • Shuffle test: Z=57.72 (0/1,000) — text-specific, not language-general NEW IN THIS VERSION (v3): 1. TRAPPED YHW MECHANISM: 2.0% of Torah tokens contain a YHW letter trapped inside roots. Removing it reveals deeper roots (e.g., אהב→אב love=father, איב→אב enemy=father, זהב→זב gold=flow). Semantic classification: י=individuation, ה=direction, ו=state-change. Verse coherence improves +11.9%, with 90.9% of cases improving and 0% worsening. 2. LETTER MEM ANALYSIS: מ functions as an "object-maker" — 68.1% of מ-prefix words transform verbs into nouns (קדש→מקדש, שפט→משפט). Three distinct functions identified with different definite-article behavior. 3. CROSS-SACRED-TEXT COMPARISON: Four sacred texts analyzed with identical methodology: • Torah (Biblical Hebrew): Z = 44.1 — EXTREME structural constraint • New Testament (Koine Greek, SBLGNT): Z = 28.8 — HIGH (non-Semitic!) • Quran (Classical Arabic, Uthmani): Z = 17.0 — SIGNIFICANT • Biblical Aramaic (Daniel): Z = 0.39 — NOT SIGNIFICANT The Torah achieves 2.7× stronger clustering than the Quran with fewer letters (22 vs 28+) and produces 41% more vocabulary diversity from a smaller corpus. 4. PURE YHW ROOTS: The Hebrew time system (היה/הוה/יהיה/אהיה) is built entirely from YHW letters. The divine name יהוה contains all three YHW letters. 5. RECALCULATED NUMBERS: All prediction metrics recalculated on full gold standard (98,122 pairs, 386 semantic groups, 5-fold CV). PACKAGE CONTENTS (8 files): 1. (Optional) Quran/NT comparison data files All data sourced exclusively from Sefaria.org API (Torah) and AlQuran.cloud API (Quran). New Testament from morphgnt/SBLGNT (GitHub). Complete code provided. texto: Robust Wildlife Detection Using Objectness-Aware Yolo with Attention and Pose Estimation. In recent years, object detectors based on deep learning have significantly advanced wildlife monitoring by automating identification of animals in diverse and challenging environments. However, existing models, including You Only Look Once (YOLOv3) and Objectness Aware YOLO (OAYOLO), struggle to detect small, occluded, or visually complex animals because of limited spatial focus, fixed label assignment, and lack of structural awareness. To address these limitations, an Attention and Pose-Aware OA-YOLO (APA-OA-YOLO) framework is proposed for robust wildlife detection. Initially, the model used a custom-built wildlife dataset, followed by enhanced spatial discrimination by integrating Convolutional Block Attention Modules (CBAM) into the DarkNet53 backbone and a feature fusion neck. Furthermore, the objectness-aware decoupled head is retained to introduce a refined objectness definition combining the Intersection over Union (IoU) and classification confidence. Subsequently, the natural break label assignment (NBLA) strategy is applied for adaptive anchor classification, incorporating assistant samples into objectness-weighted classification loss. Furthermore, a lightweight pose estimation branch predicts animal key points and uses pose information with detection features for refined bounding box prediction. The experimental results demonstrate that APA-OA-YOLO achieves an improved detection performance with an Average Precision (AP) of 67.8 %, True Positive Rate (TPR) of$\mathbf{8 4. 1 \%}$, and recall of$\mathbf{8 5. 1 \%}$. wildlife detection animal pose estimation attention mechanism CBAM occluded object detection small object detection Darknet-53 wildlife monitoring

texto: Clinical and ultrasonographic correlation of changes in the equine axial skeleton with thoracic and pelvic lameness detected by objective evaluation. Cervical and thoracolumbar changes are commonly found in sports animals and may be related to biomechanical alterations, driving movement, and the type of saddle used. The objective of this study was to characterize the correlation between clinical and ultrasonographic findings of the equine axial skeleton with objective evaluation lameness in the thoracic or pelvic limbs. A total of 76 horses of the mounted cavalry with an average of ten years of age, divided between castrated males and females of indeterminate breeds, were submitted to clinical, ultrasonographic and objective evaluations. The evaluated variables were classified in scores from 0 to 4, for later statistical analysis spearman correlation through the RStudio® software. The animals were classified into six groups according to the objective, clinical and ultrasonographic changes. A weak positive correlation was observed between the objective evaluation variable in relation to the clinical (r = 0.1, p > 0,05) and ultrasonographic (r = 0.1, p > 0,05) evaluation variables. In the present study, it was impossible to consider the correlations statistically significant since the p-value was higher than the significance level of 5%. Therefore, the associated evaluation of the axial and appendicular skeleton is of fundamental importance in the clinical routine to investigate musculoskeletal changes. This was demonstrated in the present study, where 68.42% (n=52) presented both clinical and ultrasonographic changes of the axial skeleton concomitantly with thoracic and/or pelvic lameness. horses musculoskeletal changes cervical spine thoracolumbar spine ultrasonography

texto: The Use of DLC for Markerless Tracking on the American Cockroach. Tracking data can be a lengthy process and tracking with the usage of markers can take an extensive amount of time. Without the usage of makers, tracking objects may take an even longer time to process the data. Processing a single trial, depending on the experiment, may take up to hours or even days to complete. This is where Deeplabcut (DLC) can come in handy. DLC is a toolbox for markerless pose estimation of animals performing various tasks. With this efficient toolbox, it is possible to track the heading variations on the American cockroach while they rapidly traverse along a rod. With the use of DLC, we are able to track the tips of their heads and abdomen to determine the effect of heading variations on rotations of the center of mass about the long axis of a rod. The usage of DLC during tracking can significantly decrease the amount of time spent digitizing data. The accuracy of DLC depends on the conditions of each trial and how the videos of these trials are taken. texto: Visually guided flight in Harris' hawks: a computer vision approach. Animals with well-developed visual systems often use vision as an active sense. This means they can manipulate the position and orientation of their viewpoint to interrogate their visual environment. In this thesis, I investigate active vision in a particularly challenging scenario: birds in manoeuvring flight. I focus on Harris' hawks (Parabuteo unicinctus), which strongly rely on vision to coordinate their manoeuvres. I cover three key challenges of studying birds' gaze strategies in flight. First, I explore the problem of accurately tracking an animal's gaze direction. Marker-based motion capture is the most accurate species-agnostic method to track 3D movements in humans and animals, but commercial systems often underperform when applied to animals. I present a marker-labelling method that solves many of the existing problems, based on an arrangement of markers that is optimal for a custom per-frame labelling algorithm. Second, I explore how to capture the visual scene an animal experiences. I solve this computationally, using a 3D model of the flight environment, and a model of the birds' view during flight. I demonstrate how the proposed method allows us to define alternative gaze strategies for hypothesis testing, and explore different methods of modelling the environment, that adapt to varying levels of geometric complexity. Third, I investigate how we can use the generated synthetic data to analyse the hawks' behaviour. For N = 4 birds, I generate semantic maps of the visual scene the animals experience in flight, for a total of n = 97 perching and obstacle avoidance flights. I characterise the birds' gaze strategies around the landing perch and the obstacles, and discuss possible explanations as to why these strategies may be advantageous. Overall, my thesis demonstrates a novel and reliable method of investigating avian vision in flight and opens up new avenues for data-driven models of animal behaviour. texto: Analyzing the Imitation Behaviors of Gorilla Chest-Beating Based on Human Pose Estimation. In animal exercise classes course for acting majors, students enhance their physical flexibility and expressiveness by imitating the behaviors and actions of various animals. The gorilla's chest-beating action is a common exercise in this course. The accuracy of students' body postures when imitating animals often depends on the instructor's experience and personal preferences, leading to students with different levels and physical characteristics not receiving targeted guidance and practice. Human pose estimation technology is already quite mature, and we hope to apply it to animal exercise courses to analyze students' body movements when imitating animals, such as chest-beating. Therefore, this paper utilizes Mediapipe technology to detect the elbow joint angles of students imitating the gorilla's chest-beating action, a two-way analysis of variance (ANOVA) was employed to examine the effects of experience and gender on joint angle variations. Additionally, the results of the U-test analyzing the differences between the gorilla and the participants confirmed that male students' elbow joint angles are closer to those of the gorilla than those of female students when mimicking the gorilla's chest-beating action. This has significant implications for improving the precision and personalization of performance training, and it also provides valuable insights for further research and practice in related fields. animal imitation human pose estimation elbow angle actor training gender differences MediaPipe

texto: Assessment of the Lame Horse. This chapter provides a thorough introduction to the assessment of the lame horse, including history, visual exam, palpation, subjective and objective assessments of lameness, perineural anesthesia, and intrasynovial anesthesia. Lameness is an indication of a structural or functional disorder in one or more limbs or the axial skeleton that is evident while the horse is standing or at movement. The majority of lameness problems in horses occur in the forelimb due to the increased weight-bearing on the forelimbs and the shock of landing that the forelimbs absorb during movement. The initial part of a lameness evaluation is a visual examination of the horse standing squarely on a flat surface at rest. Palpation of the musculoskeletal system is a very important aspect of the lameness evaluation and with experience, subtle abnormalities can be detected that are often indicative of the site of the problem. equine lameness lameness assessment horses visual inspection forelimb lameness

texto: Equine Musculoskeletal and Lameness Exams. Evaluating the musculoskeletal system and performing a lameness examination are routine clinical procedures for the equine practitioner. Both play an essential role in assessing the health and well-being of horses, particularly performance horses, and can be diagnostic for a variety of ailments that impact bone, cartilage, muscle, ligaments, and tendons. Lameness in and of itself is not a disease, but rather a clinical sign, that requires additional investigation by the practitioner to determine its source. The veterinary practitioner will often begin with observation of the patient at rest followed by palpation of the large muscle groups. Visual and tactile assessment of limbs in weight-bearing and non-weight-bearing positions are an essential part of the systematic approach to lameness assessment. Often there is overlap between the musculoskeletal and lameness examinations. For that reason, they will be considered in tandem in this chapter. Lameness is most often caused by pain; however, lameness can be confused with neurological dysfunction. The goal of this chapter is to appreciate how the veterinarian can glean information about lameness or potential lameness by being thorough in their examination. equine lameness lameness examination musculoskeletal examination horses performance horses neurological disorders palpation limb pain

titulo: A long-term follow up study of a birth cohort of boxer dogs in The Netherlands : genetic and environmental risk factors for diseases
keywords: Boxer dog;canine hip dysplasia;cranial cruciate ligament rupture;hindlimb lameness;heritability;genetic risk factors;environmental risk factors;mesenchymal tumors;canine cancer;Mendelian inheritance;litter effects;pre-weaning mortality;castration;survival analysis;disease incidence;mortality;purebred dogs
texto: A long-term follow up study of a birth cohort of boxer dogs in The Netherlands : genetic and environmental risk factors for diseases. This thesis describes the long-term follow up of a birth cohort of boxer dogs to study disease incidence, mortality, as well as genetic and environmental risk factors in a purebred dog population in The Netherlands. During the last decades, both the number of genetic disorders and the disease rate of these disorders seemed to increase. Therefore, special attention was given to presumed genetic disorders. Heritability in this thesis was estimated using a proportional hazard model based on the Weibull distribution as implemented in the Survival Kit software. Parametric survival models were developed to identify the influence of potential risk factors. Risk factors included individual data and litter data. Between November 1999 and March 2004 a total of 1863 boxer dogs from 388 litters, all born between January 1994 and February 1995 were monitored. Data was collected by interviewing the dog-owners through self-completion (mail) questionnaires, which were sent every 6 months. At the end of the study 674 boxer dogs had survived up to that point, 530 dogs had died (including euthanasia). Survival analyses, accounting for loss to follow up, resulted in a mortality rate of 45% of the cohort of boxer dogs. The highest disease incidence in this boxer dog population was attributable to hind limb lameness of which cranial cruciate ligament rupture (22%) and canine hip dysplasia (8.5%) were most frequently diagnosed. When the box-floor was covered with slippery material, the risk of cCHD increased 1.6 times, and the risk of cCHD doubled in litters with high preweaning mortality. Castration, =6 months prior to cCHD diagnosis, increased the risk of cCHD 1.5 times. The general risk of boxer dogs developing cCHD and CCL rupture after 5 years of age was 1.8 and 2.4 times higher than before the age of 5, respectively. The effective heritability of cCHD was 11% and of CCL rupture was 16%. We described tumor and cancer incidence. Classification of skin tumors showed a high incidence of mesenchymal tumors (88%). The risk rate of developing mesenchymal tumors after 5 years of age was 43.6 times higher than before the age of 5. We studied whether or not the segregation of white spotting in the boxer dogs follows a Mendelian inheritance pattern. Because the flashy phenotype seems to be an intermediate between the two homozygotes, white spotting in the Dutch boxer dog is apparently due to a single gene effect, with incomplete dominance. We have evaluated candidate-genes c-KIT (KIT) and EDNRB for segregation with white spotting phenotype, but found that segregation of the white spotting pattern did not coincide with segregation of these polymorphic markers. Our group developed a genetic counseling program for boxer dog-breeders in the Netherlands. The goal of the study was to evaluate the use of our genetic counseling program by Dutch breeders of boxer dogs. Although it was the first time breeders could make use of genetic counseling, 32% of the breeders indicated that the genetic counseling played a major role in their sire selection. The ideal breeding schemes would select breeding animals with the best possible estimated breeding value (EBV) score while constraining their average coancestry to a predefined value. Therefore application of EBVs should be added to the standard criteria for selection decisions. Genetic counseling programs that provide an overall EBV index could facilitate the task of dog breeders to select simultaneously for several characteristics. We calculated the EBV of the 10 best and 10 worst sires to predict the risk of cCHD, CCL rupture, life expectancy and mesenchymal skin tumors, respectively, in the progeny of these sires. The results illustrated that breeding programs can be improved by the introduction of EBVs, which enable the breeder to identify the best male breeding dogs In the future, veterinarians will be able to offer an increasing number of DNA-tests to their clients. Because this DNA-testing is not sufficiently available yet, the elimination of genetic disease is hampered. In the meantime, non-DNA-based genetic-counselling can prevent spreading of hereditary disease in purebred dog populations. titulo: Reflections on “Dream of the Red Chamber” (review)
keywords: Dream of the Red Chamber;Liu Zaifu;Cao Xueqin;Wang Guowei;tragedy;spiritual realm;Arthur Schopenhauer;Chinese classical fiction;English translation;Gao Xingjian;Chinese aesthetics
texto: Reflections on “Dream of the Red Chamber” (review). Reviewed by: Reflections on “Dream of the Red Chamber” Ying Wang (bio) Liu Zaifu. Reflections on “Dream of the Red Chamber.” Translated by Shu Yunzhong. Amherst, NY: Cambria Press, 2008. xviii, 301 pp. Hardcover $109.95, ISBN 978-1-604975-24-6. The 2008 English translation of Liu Zaifu’s book Reflections on “Dream of the Red Chamber” offers a delightful, fascinating, and enlightening reading of Cao Xueqin’s eighteenth-century masterpiece Honglou meng (Dream of the red chamber). Liu’s reading, which tries to be free of the conventions of scholarship and scholarly writing, is described as an “intuitive approach of Zen” (p. xiii) by Gao Xingjian (winner of the 2000 Nobel Prize for Literature) in his foreword to the book. Consisting of casual literary notes jotted down by the author over the period of a decade and some of his topical essays written for speeches and publications, Liu’s [End Page 347] book is, indeed, unconventional in format and structure. However, the author does not take his critique of Cao Xueqin’s novel lightly, and at least two important theoretical and aesthetic questions are repeatedly raised, discussed, and expounded in this book, showing the author’s serious intention to contribute further to the scholarship of Honglou meng. Both of Liu’s questions are generated from Wang Guowei’s (1877–1927) salient study titled A Critique of “Dream of the Red Chamber.” While challenging Wang Guowei’s classification of Honglou meng as a work of mere tragedy, Liu Zaifu applauds Wang’s emphasis on the “existence of a spiritual realm” in Cao Xueqin’s novel and makes a further exploration of this “spiritual realm” the central task of his reappraisal (pp. 137–140). In his 1904 critique, Wang Guowei praises Honglou meng’s successful use of tragedy on the grounds that it is subversive to both the Chinese literary tradition and the conventional reader’s taste. Analyzing Cao Xueqin’s novel according to Schopenhauer’s three types of tragedy, Wang identifies Honglou meng as the most tragic type—in which characters “are so situated with regard to one another that their position forces them, knowingly and with their eyes open, to do one another the greatest injury without any one of them being entirely in the wrong”1—in comparison to the type of tragedy that is caused either by exceptional wickedness of a character or by a colossal accident or error. Deeply influenced by Shopenhauer’s vision of the world as a ceaseless, destructive struggle for existence, Wang Guowei’s concept of tragedy and his interpretation of the underlying philosophy of Honglou meng are permeated with a pessimistic view of life and the conviction of release (or renouncing of the world). According to Liu Zaifu, Wang’s appraisal is only partial in terms of the literary modes employed in the eighteenth-century novel. To Liu, Honglou meng is not merely a “tragedy of tragedies” as defined by Wang; it is also a work revealing absurdity in the human world—therefore, a novel of comedy with a modern flavor. As indicated by Liu, “the predominantly tragic tone in Dream of the Red Chamber is mixed with traces of the absurdity in the human world. Drama of absurdity is an extreme form of comedy. Originating from traditional comedy and yet different from traditional comedy, it displays the worthlessness and meaninglessness of life in an extreme manner. . . . [T]he absurd is not just a strategy but also an insightful and critical reference to reality” (p. 147). Cao Xueqin’s effort at revealing the absurd nature of the human world can be observed, according to Liu, from his numerous examples that mock futile pursuit of worldly gain in the novel, including allegorical verses and stories, such as “Won-Done Song,” sung by the lame Taoist priest in chapter 1; “Mandarin’s Life Preserver” in chapter 4; and “Precious Mirror of Desire” in chapter 12. There are, of course, characters of absurdity portrayed by Cao Xueqin as well. Jia Yucun, Liu claims, “constitutes the most absurd part of the novel,” as he makes absurd judgments about his life and political career as a result of being “entangled in [a] web of social relationships... keywords: major depressive disorder;cardiometabolic risk;depression subtypes;structural neuroimaging;cortical thickness;gray matter volume;white matter fractional anisotropy;suicide attempts;adverse childhood experiences;cardiovascular disease;diabetes mellitus;UK Biobank;unsupervised clustering;personalized treatment;suicide risk prediction
texto: STRUCTURAL NEUROIMAGING UNCOVERS DIFFERENT CARDIOMETABOLIC RISK PROFILES IN DEPRESSION: A DATA-DRIVEN APPROACH ON UK BIOBANK. Abstract Background Major depressive disorder (MDD) is a heterogeneous psychiatric condition associated with a high risk of mortality considering both high rates of suicide [1] and of severe comorbid cardiometabolic dysfunctions [2]. Environmental variables such as adverse childhood experiences (ACEs) can furtherly interact with the disorder’ s prognosis [3-4]. However, not all MDD patients exhibit the same illness trajectories, thus leading to inconsistent findings between clinical outcomes and the underlying neurobiology [5]. Therefore, stratifying MDD based on neurobiological data could prompt the reveal of distinct disorder subtypes and enable personalized treatment approaches. Aims & Objectives We employed an unsupervised machine learning approach to stratify MDD patients into biologically-driven clusters using multimodal structural neuroimaging data, which were then characterized for different cardiometabolic profiles, suicide attempts (SA), and ACEs. Method Cortical thickness, cortical and subcortical grey matter volumes, surface area, and white matter fractional anisotropy (FA) were extracted from 3636 individuals affected by MDD among the UK Biobank cohort. A stability-based relative clustering validation approach [6] was applied to these data to identify neurobiologically homogeneous patients’ subgroups. K-means was implemented for clustering, and support vector machine was trained to predict clusters’ labels through a 2-fold cross-validation iterated 100 times. The best clustering solution among 2 to 5 clusters was identified by minimizing the prediction error. A subsample of 727 individuals (20%) was used to optimize the model’ s hyperparameters through a parallel grid search, while the optimized pipeline was applied on the remaining 2909 (80%). Confounding effects of age, sex, and volumetric scaling factor were controlled in cross-validation. Mann-Whitney U and Chi-squared tests were used to explore differences and associations between the identified clusters and age, sex, structural neuroimaging features, BMI, presence of any cardiovascular disease, diagnosis of diabetes, history of SA, childhood emotional, physical, and sexual abuse, childhood emotional and physical neglect. Results The optimized stability-based clustering pipeline identified 2 clusters (N cluster1=1361, N cluster2=1548) with a normalized stability of 0.084, meaning that the input features could discriminate clusters’ labels with a 91.6% of accuracy. The second cluster was significantly associated with a higher prevalence of cardiovascular diseases (χ2=4.846, p=0.027), comorbid diabetes (χ2=13.245, p<0.001), and childhood physical abuse (χ2=4.101, p=0.043). Remarkably, the same cluster also showed lower cortical thickness (p<0.001), lower cortical and subcortical volumes (p<0.001), and higher surface areas (p<0.001) in most regions of interest, as well as lower FA (p<0.001) in all white matter tracts. No significant associations and differences for SA, age, sex, and BMI were found. Discussion & Conclusion Our data-driven approach revealed that structural neuroimaging can uncover depression subtypes linked to different cardiometabolic risk profiles, which were also associated with a childhood history of physical abuse. These results can hence contribute to the understanding of MDD pathophysiology and possibly help to detect vulnerable individuals which may benefit from tailored treatments in a precision psychiatry framework. texto: Adapter-Enhanced ViTPose for Occlusion-Robust Multi-Mouse Pose Estimation. Accurate pose estimation of laboratory mice is essential for automated behavior analysis. However, in confined laboratory environments, frequent interactions among mice often lead to severe inter-animal occlusions, posing significant challenges for pose estimation. Although large pretrained models such as ViTPose provide strong visual representations, adapting them to laboratory mouse scenarios is difficult due to limited annotated data. Full fine-tuning is prone to overfitting, while freezing the backbone and tuning only the decoder often yields insufficient domain adaptation.To address this issue, we investigate parameter-efficient adaptation of ViTPose using lightweight adapter modules. Specifically, we evaluate two adapter architectures, AdaptFormer and ConvPass, within a frozen ViTPose backbone, enabling effective transfer to occlusion-heavy mouse scenes with only a small number of trainable parameters. To systematically assess occlusion robustness, we further construct a synthesized multi-mouse benchmark by compositing temporally shifted mouse instances and quantifying overlap severity using mask IoU. Experiments show that adapter-based tuning consistently improves pose estimation accuracy over conventional frozen-backbone adaptation.On the synthesized multi-mouse benchmark, ConvPass improves the overall AP of ViTPose-Base from 0.736 to 0.843, and further increases AP under severe occlusion from 0.429 to 0.596. A controlled ablation shows that, when ConvPass is aligned with AdaptFormer in adapter insertion position and bottleneck dimension, ConvPass⋆improves AP over AdaptFormer from 0.804 to 0.856 under moderate occlusion and from 0.552 to 0.603 under severe occlusion. Additional results on AP-10K show that AdaptFormer and ConvPass improve AP from 0.555 to 0.688 and 0.687, respectively, further demonstrating the effectiveness of parameter-efficient adaptation for animal pose estimation. occlusion robustness ViTPose parameter-efficient fine-tuning adapters domain adaptation animal behavior analysis

titulo: The Myth of the Jewish Race: A Biologist's Point of View (review)
keywords: Jewish race;concept of race;Jewish identity;heredity (biology);secularization;Judaism;Inquisition;racism;Enlightenment;Holocaust;human races;Jewish history;ethnic identity;ancestry;Final Solution;race and science;anthropology of race;history of biology;history of anthropology;history of genetics
texto: The Myth of the Jewish Race: A Biologist's Point of View (review). Reviewed by: The Myth of the Jewish Race: A Biologist's Point of View Michael Berkowitz The Myth of the Jewish Race: A Biologist's Point of View, by Alain F. Corcos. Bethlehem: Lehigh University Press, 2005. 170 pp. $39.50. With the best of intentions Alain Corcos, a biologist, seeks to bury—for all time—the ludicrous myth that Jews constitute a "race." The crux of his argument is certainly convincing, and his further challenge to the terms "Jewish blood" and "Jewish genes" is an important corrective to ideas that have lingered even among a few post-Holocaust Jewish scholars. But is this book, even as brief as it is, justified as a monograph? It would have been better as a journal article or part of an anthology. As much as Corcos is deft in applying biology to Jews, therefore handily debunking the myth of a Jewish race, he is far less adept in his control of Jewish history. He has virtually no understanding of ethnic and religious identity as conceived by historians and social scientists, instead embracing a view of Jewry based on too narrow a definition of Judaism (p. 72). Corcos does not see that different cultural forms, which came to be associated with Jews and Judaism, developed around the practice of Judaism. Perhaps most seriously, the author underestimates the extent to which processes of secularization were ways of transforming and even preserving Jewishness (pp. 18ff.). In other words, he is excellent on race (pp. 126–8), as understood biologically, but clumsy on identity. His chapter on "Spain and the Concept of the Jewish Race" does not recognize that racism arose concomitant to the Enlightenment, and the persecution of the Inquisition derived from a simplistic notion of heredity allowing for numerous exceptions that would have been anathema to Nazi racism. "Whatever the reason," Corcos states, "the result was clearly a preview of the Holocaust" (p. 37). Here he commits the historical gaffe of reading backwards. Given his quest for precision, it is surprising that he conflates "ancestry" with [End Page 215] racism (p. 39). His synopsis of "Science and the Concept of the Jewish Race" and recounting of "The Final Solution" are solid but offer nothing new. The strongest sections of this book, not surprisingly, are those that deal with human races generally. Corcos would go so far as to replace the term race with "deme," denoting "groupings." "No matter how many [racial] groups we propose, we always find people who do not fit any one category. Racial classification is impossible because humanity is very diverse, and distinct lines of demarcation among groups do not exist." Nevertheless, there exists some "resemblance within groups," that results mainly from intramarriage (p. 71). His discussion of skin color related to supposed racial groups and demolition of the concepts of "Jewish Blood, Genes, and Diseases" are brief but compelling (pp. 73–8). The author's attempt to read Jewish history with an eye toward demonstrating the extent to which Jews mixed with surrounding non-Jewish populations, through sexual relations and proselytism, is commendable. His treatment of Ethiopia and China, however, ignores recent scholarship, such as that of Daniel Summerfield and Zhou Xun, which calls into question the notion that Jews in these regions "practiced for centuries a pre-rabbinic form of Judaism" (p. 102). Likewise, there are number of problems in his summaries of German, Russian, Soviet, and American Jewish history. Despite these many reservations, this book will come in handy as a hard-science rejoinder to lame-brained students and cranks who invariably show up at public lectures with the stupid and dangerous contention that Jews are a race. texto: Prediction and detection of bone rupture during an osteotomy using an instrumented mallet. Prédiction et détection de la rupture d’un os lors d’une ostéotomie à l’aide d’un maillet instrumenté Les ostéotomies sont des interventions chirurgicales visant à couper les tissus osseux ou cartilagineux afin de les remodeler ou de les réaligner. Lors de l'ostéotomie, le chirurgien utilise un maillet pour frapper un instrument chirurgical composé d’une lame et d'un manche, appelé ostéotome. Les décisions prises pendant l'opération sont uniquement basées sur la proprioception du chirurgien, c'est-à-dire le son et le retour haptique et sont donc subjectives et dépendantes de l'expérience du chirurgien. Ce travail porte sur le développement d'une technique vibroacoustique, un maillet instrumenté, pour détecter et prévenir la rupture de l'os en temps réel pendant une ostéotomie.Dans une étude préliminaire, la méthode vibroacoustique a été utilisée pour détecter la rupture d’échantillons en forme de plaque composé de différents matériaux. Ensuite, des protocoles spécifiques basés sur la même méthode vibroacoustique ont été développés et appliqués à des ostéotomies utilisées en pratique clinique.La méthode a d'abord été appliquée à une partie spécifique de l'ostéotomie de Le Fort, la rupture des plaques ptérygoïdes également appelée disjonction ptérygomaxillaire. Cette ostéotomie étant réalisée sans contrôle visuel, des hémorragies et des lésions nerveuses peuvent survenir si des impacts supplémentaires inutiles sont donnés. Des disjonctions ptérygomaxillaires ont été réalisées sur un modèle animal, en utilisant des têtes d'agneau et sur des sujets anatomiques. Un algorithme de classification, une machine à vecteurs de support combinée à une matrice de coût, a été appliqué aux informations extraites du signal de chaque impact afin de détecter la rupture des plaques.Ensuite, la méthode a été appliquée à l'ostéotomie tibiale de valgisation. Dans cette ostéotomie, le chirurgien coupe le tibia et crée une charnière pour réaligner le plateau tibial. Pour éviter la rupture de la charnière et donc de l'os, le chirurgien doit arrêter d’impacter dès que la pointe de l’ostéotome atteint l'os cortical. Un critère basé sur les informations recueillies par le maillet instrumenté a été développé et appliqué à la détection de la transition de l'os cortical à l'os trabéculaire et vice versa. Le protocole a été validé sur des tibias de porc et sur des sujets anatomiques.Cette thèse démontre que le maillet instrumenté basé sur l’analyse vibroacoustique, peut être utilisé pour détecter la rupture de l’os. De plus, comme la capacité de prédire et de détecter la rupture peut être utile à d'autres chirurgies, cette méthode a été étendue à d’autres applications, telles que l'élévation du sinus maxillaire et la pose de vis pédiculaires. Ces derniers résultats ont été obtenus dans le cadre de collaborations internationales. texto: Approach to the Lame Horse. Lameness is common in all types of horse and is defined as an alteration in the animal’s normal stance and/or mode of progression caused by pain or neural or mechanical dysfunction. The approach to the lame horse should ideally be carried out in a logical sequence in order to (1) define which limb or limbs are involved and (2) find the exact site of pain. Only then can other techniques such as radiography or more advanced imaging (e.g. bone scintigraphy or MRI) be used to determine a specific pathological process and make a diagnosis. Once a provisional or accurate diagnosis is made, a management plan can be formulated and a prognosis given to the owner. In practice, many factors may alter this sequence slightly (e.g. the environment where the examination is taking place, financial considerations, impending competition). equine lameness lameness diagnosis radiography bone scintigraphy magnetic resonance imaging prognosis equine management
